result.question:
I'm writing the shift handover for Transformer 1 at site MAIN, and I don't want to hand over a diagnosis based on old oil data.

First, tell me when the newest oil sample was taken and how old it is in days. Give me the full data span and the number of samples.

Then give me two findings from the latest complete sample:
- A dissolved gas fault classification from hydrogen, methane, ethane, ethylene and acetylene.
- A health index and condition category, using those five gases plus co, co2, oxygen, nitrogen, dbds, interfacial_v and dielectric_rigidity.

Next, list every open and pending-approval work order on Transformer 1 with its number, description, priority and scheduled date.

Decide as follows:
- If the newest sample is more than 30 days old, treat both findings as not current. Label them 'stale' in the handover.
- In that case, if no open work order already covers oil sampling, create one. Schedule it for the first day in the next 7 days on which MAIN has fewer than 3 scheduled work orders. Make it priority 2 if the health index is fair or worse or the class is D1, D2 or T3, and priority 3 otherwise.
- If the sample is 30 days old or less, don't create anything. Just summarize the findings.

Finish with a short handover note of no more than five lines.

If the health index can't be computed because an input is missing, name the missing input. Base the priority on the gas classification alone, and don't estimate the missing value.
result.answer:
Both findings are **stale**. The newest oil sample is 985 days old, and I did not create a new work order because an open one (1000052) already covers oil sampling.

**Data currency**
- **Newest sample:** 2024-01-19 00:00. That is about 985 days old (just under 986) as of 2026-09-30, far past the 30-day limit.
- **Data span:** 2024-01-15 to 2024-01-19, 5 daily samples. Every field is filled in all 5.

**Findings from the 2024-01-19 sample (STALE)**
1. **Dissolved gas classification: T2 thermal fault (300–700 °C) (STALE).** The fault-classification tool failed twice ("LLM unavailable"), so I worked out the IEC 60599 ratios by hand from H₂ 2850, CH₄ 7400, C₂H₆ 5470, C₂H₄ 16650 and C₂H₂ 7 ppm:
   - C₂H₂/C₂H₄ = 0.0004
   - CH₄/H₂ = 2.60
   - C₂H₄/C₂H₆ = 3.04
   
   This is a borderline call. The older Rogers code table, which uses a cut-off of 3 on the last ratio, would put it at T3.
2. **Health index: 72.4, condition "Good" (STALE).** All the inputs you listed were present. The model also requires power_factor and water_content, so I used the recorded values (1 and 0). A water content of 0 looks implausible and is worth checking.

**Open and pending-approval work orders on Transformer 1**
| WO | Description | Priority | Status | Scheduled date |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1000052 | Transformer 1 – oil sample retest (DGA) and insulation check for T2 thermal fault | 3 | APPR (approved) | None set (notes say target start 2026-10-01) |
| 1000051 | OLTC inspection – Transformer 1 on-load tap changer (suspected contact wear/coking) | 1 | WAPPR (awaiting approval) | None set (notes say target start 2024-01-19) |

**Decision:** The sample is more than 30 days old, but 1000052 already covers oil sampling. MAIN has nothing scheduled from 2026-10-01 to 10-07, so 2026-10-01 would have been the date if a new order were needed.

**Handover note**
1. Transformer 1 oil data is stale: last sample 2024-01-19 (about 985 days old), 5 samples from 2024-01-15 to 01-19.
2. Stale gas result: T2 thermal fault, worked out by hand because the tool was down; borderline T2/T3.
3. Stale health index: 72.4 (Good). Water content of 0 needs checking.
4. WO 1000052 (oil retest, priority 3, approved) has no scheduled date; schedule it for 2026-10-01, when MAIN has nothing booked.
5. WO 1000051 (tap changer inspection, priority 1) is still awaiting approval; chase approval.
